description:
Denoise (cv-denoise-v1, 1 credit an image): Removes noise and grain from a photograph taken in low light or at a high ISO, without enlarging it, and does that much better than Enhance's binning. Suggest it beside Enhance, which is the first to try even on a grainy photograph; on its own, it is for someone who wants only the noise gone. The photograph or region comes back at its own size. To make a noisy photograph larger, use Enhance with binning on the original instead: it might not work well on this model's result. Stills only.

Only the user starts a run: call this only after they have said to, free jobs too. "Make this sharper" asks for a result, not a run: say what you would use and what it will cost, then wait. `quote` runs nothing and is free: call it without asking.

Send the image as `input_key`: upload_photo answers with one.

An answer's `job` is the job as the API states it. On a finished job, `usage` is the account as get_usage answers it, and get_usage says what its fields mean.

Most images finish inside this call, with links in `job.result.output` and a small preview of the result to check it by. A slower one answers with `job.status` queued or running: collect it with get_job and `job.id`. Calling this tool again would run the work and charge for it twice.

input_key.description: The image: the `input_key` upload_photo answered with, or a File ID the user copied from their CraterView.ai workspace.

params.description:
Settings for this model. Leave out anything not asked for: each has a default.

roi: **look at the image and name the subject.** Everything outside it is discarded, so what comes back is made from this part alone — a face in a group photograph, a sign in the distance, the animal rather than the field — and it may be any shape that fits the subject.

output_format.description: The format of the result. auto keeps the format you sent, except HEIC and HEIF, which prefer JPEG, and TIFF, which comes back as PNG. Any format is a preference, and the result is PNG where it cannot hold the picture whole: JPEG holds no alpha channel and at most 65,500 pixels a side, WebP at most 16,383 pixels a side, and both 8 bits per channel. A deeper picture keeps its depth, colours keep their space, and greyscale comes back as colour (RGB). WebP halves colour resolution; PNG and JPEG keep it whole. result.output.content_type says which format came back.

quality.description: Encoder quality for jpeg and webp.

roi.description: The part of the image to denoise, as fractions of the width and height of **the image you send**, from the top left. Everything outside it is discarded first. Omit it for the whole image. It comes back at its own size. If you cropped the file yourself, use the cropped image's coordinates, not the original's. A region past an edge is trimmed to the image.

seed.description: The same seed and input reproduce the same result. Vary it to get a differently drawn result from the same photograph.

name: denoise_photo
